top_drivers.driver: CGC Week 38 exports were 379.2 Ktonnes and rose 38.4% week over week while producer deliveries rose 6.6%, giving the frozen snapshot a bullish commercial-pull signal.
Producer deliveries were 433.3 Ktonnes and exports equaled 87.5% of weekly deliveries, while the source read also preserved domestic crush as a separate demand pull.
Grain Monitor context showed 20 vessels waiting at Vancouver, 71% terminal capacity, and aligned Week 38 logistics timing, which supports a firm physical-flow read rather than a loose logistics read.

Managed-money net position of 89,108 contracts and an ICE Canola futures sample at 743.2 CAD/tonne are supportive context, but CFTC proxy mapping and price-source warnings keep this below a high-confidence price call.

The exporter redacted or omitted unadmitted/private, posted-price, weather, and WASDE lanes, so the thesis should be judged first by next-week public movement evidence rather than broad outside context.

invalidating_triggers: Next CGC movement evidence shows exports and producer deliveries falling enough to erase the Week 38 commercial-pull signal.
Grain Monitor logistics context loosens materially, with vessel pressure or terminal capacity no longer supporting the bullish read.
A verified ICE Canola RSN26 settlement refresh contradicts the bullish thesis after the forecast cutoff.
A direct Canola COT update weakens the managed-money support once proxy rows are separated from direct Canola truth.
